---
id: SA-0412
title: "_host_survivor_cell's own docstring takes the perfect tense CLAUDE.md bans, past the gate's own regex"
type: bug
priority: 4
estimated_lines: 16
estimate_measured: true
touches:
  - tests/test_session.py
forbidden:
  - DESIGN.md
  - CONTEXT.md
  - CLAUDE.md
  - README.md
  - pyproject.toml
  - uv.lock
  - .saffron/**
  - .claude/**
  - ontology/**
  - tests/ontology/**
  - docs/**
  - images/**
  - harness/**
  - records/**
  - hooks/**
  - saffron/**
  - tests/test_review.py
  - tests/test_rebut.py
budget_usd: 10
max_attempts: 2
max_turns: 40
acceptance:
  - claim: >-
      `tests/test_session.py:18219`, inside `_host_survivor_cell`'s own
      docstring, reads "exported patch `_GROWN_PATCH` once the rebuttal
      turn has run, and". CLAUDE.md's own prose rule, at CLAUDE.md:238-239,
      lets no new comment or docstring take the perfect tense. "has run"
      is the perfect tense of "run". `.saffron/gates/prose.py`'s own
      `PERFECT` pattern, at line 97, matches only "has/have/had been" or
      "has/have" paired with a word ending "-ed". "run" ends in no "-ed",
      so the gate reports this line clean regardless. The witness reads
      `_host_survivor_cell.__doc__` straight from the live function and
      refuses "has", "have" or "had" paired with "run" with or without
      "already" between the two words, caught by that pattern or not,
      and pins the exact replacement phrase "once the rebuttal turn
      runs" in its place.
    witness: tests/test_session.py::test_the_host_survivor_cells_own_docstring_takes_no_perfect_tense
---

## Context

Reviewer finding on `SA-0407` (saffron SA-0407, `6a8cc298`). The line number
below is read at this stack's head, `6a8cc2981f896926f3d7d005c70b61a81d7101f2`.

`tests/test_session.py:18207-18221` defines `_host_survivor_cell`. Its
docstring, at lines 18216-18221, reads in part at line 18219: "exported
patch `_GROWN_PATCH` once the rebuttal turn has run, and". `git blame`
charges this text to `SA-0407`'s own commit `bf46dc8d1`. The text is new
there, not carried over from an earlier spec.

CLAUDE.md:238-239 states the house rule. New Markdown and new comments
take no em-dash, semicolon, contraction, perfect tense, hedge or sentence
over 25 words, in CLAUDE.md's own words. "has run" is the present perfect
of the irregular verb "run". This line breaks that rule on its own terms.

`.saffron/gates/prose.py:97` defines the pattern the `prose` gate checks
this against: `PERFECT = re.compile(r"\b(?:has|have|had)\s+been\b|\b(?:has|have)\s+\w+ed\b", re.I)`.
The second branch wants a word ending "-ed" right after "has" or "have".
"run" is its own past participle. It ends in no "-ed". Neither branch
matches "has run". The gate's own run over this file today reports no hit
on line 18219, measured by calling `.saffron/gates/prose.py`'s own `check`
function directly on `tests/test_session.py`'s text.

## Problem

Reword `tests/test_session.py:18219` so the clause reads in the present
tense instead of the perfect one. Add a witness that reads
`_host_survivor_cell`'s own docstring, and fails on the construction this
line carries today, caught by the gate's own pattern or not.

1. **The reword.** Change "once the rebuttal turn has run, and" to "once
   the rebuttal turn runs, and". No other word in the docstring changes.
2. **The witness.** Add a test reading `_host_survivor_cell.__doc__`
   straight from the function object. It refuses "has run", "have run"
   and "had run", with or without "already" between the two words. It
   also asserts the corrected phrase "once the rebuttal turn runs" sits
   in the docstring's text.

## Out of scope

- **`.saffron/gates/prose.py`'s own `PERFECT` pattern.** `.saffron/**` is
  a protected path here. This spec's own `forbidden` list names
  `saffron/**` too, so no change reaches the gate or any production
  module. The fix is the one docstring's wording, and a test that reads
  it directly, not a wider gate rule.
- **Every other "has run" phrase already in `tests/test_session.py`.**
  `git blame` charges several to specs that landed before `SA-0407`.
  CLAUDE.md's "new" qualifier never reached them, and this spec's own
  finding names only line 18219. A later spec can take up the rest on its
  own finding.
- **`tests/test_review.py` and `tests/test_rebut.py`.** Both sit in this
  spec's allowed set, and both are named in `forbidden` too. The one line
  this spec corrects lives only in `tests/test_session.py`.
- **Any runtime behaviour of `_host_survivor_cell` or the three tests
  that call it.** The function's body, its parameters and every call site
  stay as they are. Only the docstring's wording and the new witness
  change.

## Notes for the agent

**The fix is new text, not a changed behaviour**, so the one criterion
declares a witness and no mutant, and `witness` reports it `skip`. The
corrected wording does not exist at base to pin a mutant against.

**No `wrong_versions` is declared either.** This spec's only touched
path is `tests/test_session.py`, a declared test path under
`policy.yaml`'s `test_paths`. `saffron/probe.py:156-169`'s
`probe_refusal` refuses any edit whose file matches a test path. An
edit of this line would be refused outright, and read as none
expressed. The claim above instead states, in its own words, the
three builds the witness must still catch.

**At base the witness fails.** Measured directly, with the docstring left
at "has run":
`assert re.search(r"\b(?:has|have|had)\s+(?:already\s+)?run\b", doc, re.I) is None`
raises, since the pattern finds the match at the span the original text
sits in.

**Check the docstring's own text, not the gate's report.** A check
against `.saffron/gates/prose.py`'s own report on this file passes
today, before any edit. That report already misses this case. The
gate's own pattern never catches "has run". The witness reads
`_host_survivor_cell.__doc__` directly instead, so it judges the
words themselves.

**Pin the exact phrase, not only the pattern's absence.** A pattern
written for "run" alone clears on other perfect-tense phrasing. One
example is "once the rebuttal turn has finished running". The second
assertion, that "once the rebuttal turn runs" sits in the docstring,
catches that case too. Measured on a prototype: a version of the
witness carrying only the pattern check passed against that one
rewording.

**`import re` is new to `tests/test_session.py`.** Add it among the
other standard-library imports at the top of the file. It sits in the
same alphabetical run as `json` and `shutil`.

**Size.** `size_gate` leaves out every block under `tests/**`
(`.saffron/policy.yaml:70`, `saffron/gates/core/size.py:286-292`).
`tests/test_session.py` is not in `elevate_on`, so this spec stays
`risk: standard`, where the size gate's own check stays advisory. Measured anyway,
with `size_gate`'s own token counter run directly on the diff: 83 changed
tokens, against the `bug` ceiling of 1300.

**The `prose` gate** reads every new comment and docstring in this diff
too, `.saffron/specs/` included. Write none with an em-dash, a semicolon,
a contraction, the perfect tense or a sentence over 25 words. The line
this spec corrects is the one case where that rule, not the gate's own
pattern, is the standard to meet.
